drafted_from: tool:trade-a-youtube-sign-in-code-for-its-tokens's row in tools/connect-a-service-and-seal-its-key/tool-rows.json (job, description, input_schema, invoke) and the folder's test/connect-by-signing-in.test.mjs, whose stand-in answers give the reply and the held word
start_here: Say to your AI: "Trade a YouTube sign-in code for its tokens for the new connection service_connection:youtube:5b7e2d10 with the code made-up-code-4f9a2c." It runs tool:trade-a-youtube-sign-in-code-for-its-tokens and tells you the tokens are kept in the vault without showing any of them.
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it sends one request to YouTube for the connection it is handed and keeps the tokens in the vault as that connection's fields.
instructions: 1. Do not run this by hand: tool:connect-an-account-by-signing-in-to-the-service runs it for you at the sign-in callback, after you open the sign-in address it gave you. Start that tool first (its kit shows the call) and keep the connection_id it answers: service_connection:youtube:5b7e2d10 is the shape.

2. To run this step alone, the AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:trade-a-youtube-sign-in-code-for-its-tokens and the input the worked example shows (the connection by its handle only, the code the service handed back, the callback address the sign-in was started with and the PKCE verifier).

3. Read what comes back: the service's reply with every kept token already replaced by the word [held]. The access, refresh and id tokens now sit in the vault as the connection's own fields; none is in the answer.
4. A refusal (a used-up code, a wrong callback address) is shown as the service's own error; nothing is kept, so start the sign-in again for a new link.

worked_examples.title: Trade a YouTube sign-in code for its tokens for a made-up connection
worked_examples.ask: Trade a YouTube sign-in code for its tokens for service_connection:youtube:5b7e2d10.
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/connect-a-service-and-seal-its-key/tool-rows.json (the row posts to oauth2.googleapis.com/token and keeps access_token, refresh_token and id_token as fields of the youtube connection) and the held word "[held]" the tests use in test/connect-by-signing-in.test.mjs; the scope is the youtube descriptor's own in records.json. Input: {"connection":{"connection_id":"service_connection:youtube:5b7e2d10"},"code":"made-up-code-4f9a2c","redirect_uri":"https://app.gettrillion.ai/work/api/connect/callback","code_verifier":"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ABCDEFG"}.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"access_token":"[held]","refresh_token":"[held]","id_token":"[held]","expires_in":3599,"scope":"openid https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube.upload https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube.readonly","token_type":"Bearer"}. The access, refresh and id tokens now sit in the vault as the connection's own fields; none is in the answer.
